problem:
Suppose we wish to approximate the solution to an initial value problem using the following numerical method:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =({x}^{2}+\sqrt{y})\cdot Δx \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy\end{aligned}
$$

If the exact solution is ${y}_{\text{exact}}(x)={x}^{2}+4x+5,$ find an expression for the local truncation error for the step from $x$ to ${x}_{\text{new}}=x+Δx.$

examples.knowledge_point: Writing an Expression for the LTE for a Given Numerical Method
examples.problem:
Suppose we wish to approximate the solution to an initial value problem using Euler's method:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & ={y}^{′}\cdot Δx \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy\end{aligned}
$$

If the exact solution is $y_{\textrm{exact}}(x) = x^3,$ find an expression for the local truncation error for the step from $x$ to $x_\text{new} = x + \Delta x.$
examples.worked_solution:
The local truncation error (LTE) is the error made in a *single step* of a numerical method, when the step begins from an *exact value*. The LTE of a numerical method at step $n$ from $x$ with exact value $y_{\textrm{exact}}(x)$ to $x_\text{new} = x + \Delta x$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{τ}_{n} & ={y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}})-{y}_{\text{new}} \\  & ={y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}})-({y}_{\text{exact}}(x)+Δy).\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that the exact solution of the initial value problem is $y_{\textrm{exact}}(x) = x^3.$ Now, let's find the $y$-increment given by the numerical method.

First, the slope at a step starting at $x$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{exact}}^{′}(x)=({x}^{3})^{′}=3{x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the increment given by the numerical method is

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & ={y}_{\text{exact}}^{′}(x)\cdot Δx \\  & =3{x}^{2}\cdot Δx.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the exact value at $x_\text{new}{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}}) & ={y}_{\text{exact}}(x+Δx) \\  & =(x+Δx)^{3} \\  & ={x}^{3}+3{x}^{2}\cdot Δx+3x\cdot (Δx)^{2}+(Δx)^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the LTE for step $n$ starting at $x{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{τ}_{n} & ={y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}})-({y}_{\text{exact}}(x)+Δy) \\  & =[{x}^{3}+3{x}^{2}\cdot Δx+3x\cdot (Δx)^{2}+(Δx)^{3}]-[{x}^{3}+3{x}^{2}\cdot Δx] \\  & ={x}^{3}-{x}^{3}+(3{x}^{2}-3{x}^{2})\cdot Δx+3x\cdot (Δx)^{2}+(Δx)^{3} \\  & =3x\cdot (Δx)^{2}+(Δx)^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=3y,\,y(0)=1
$$

Suppose we wish to approximate the solution using Euler's method:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & ={y}^{′}\cdot Δx \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the exact solution is ${y}_{\text{exact}}(x)={e}^{3x},$ compute the local truncation error ${τ}_{1}$ for the first step starting at $x=0$ with step size $Δx=0.2.$ Round your answer to three decimal places.

feedback.worked_solution:
The local truncation error (LTE) is the error made in a *single step* of a numerical method, when the step begins from an *exact value*. The LTE of a numerical method at step $n$ from $x$ with exact value ${y}_{\text{exact}}(x)$ to ${x}_{\text{new}}=x+Δx$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{τ}_{n} & ={y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}})-{y}_{\text{new}} \\  & ={y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}})-({y}_{\text{exact}}(x)+Δy).\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that the exact $y$-value at the start of the step $x=0$ is $y(0)=1.$  Now, let's find the $y$-increment given by the numerical method.

First, the slope at the start of the step is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{exact}}^{′}(0) & =3{y}_{\text{exact}}(0) \\  & =3\cdot 1 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the increment at this step is

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & ={y}_{\text{exact}}^{′}(0)\cdot Δx \\  & =3\cdot 0.2 \\  & =0.6.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the exact value at ${x}_{\text{new}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}}) & ={y}_{\text{exact}}(x+Δx) \\  & ={y}_{\text{exact}}(0+0.2) \\  & ={y}_{\text{exact}}(0.2) \\  & ={e}^{3\cdot 0.2} \\  & ={e}^{0.6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the LTE for the first step starting at $x=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{τ}_{1} & ={y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}})-(y(0)+Δy) \\  & ={e}^{0.6}-(1+0.6) \\  & ={e}^{0.6}-1.6 \\  & ≈0.222\end{aligned}
$$
